newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 6-month TEM yield falls to 19.54 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 6-month TEM yield falls to 19.54 pct.

text.p: Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEMs fell 87 basis points to 19.54 percent in Wednesday's auction, according to a calculation by Reuters that uses the Central Bank formula.

The Central Bank said it sold 70 billion bolivars of 177- day "monetary stabilization", or TEM, bills with a 20.42 percent coupon for a price of 100.3929 pct. At last week's auction, the six-month notes yielded 20.42 percent.

The bank also sold 25 billion bolivars of 268-day notes VE9MTMA=RR with a 20.94 percent coupon at a price of 99.5537 percent, and 25 billion bolivars of 358-day notes VE1YTMA=RR with a 21.47 percent coupon at an average price of 99.1283 percent.
Yields for these notes fell 113 basis points to 21.64 percent for 268-day bills, and 118 basis points to 22.54 percent for the 358-day TEMs.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
